title: The Epidemiological Characteristics and Spatiotemporal Clustering of Measles - China, 2005-2022.
ehr_evidence: We utilized data from the China Disease Prevention and Control Information System for our comprehensive analysis.
summary: Spatiotemporal and epidemiological analysis of measles incidence trends and clustering in China from 2005 to 2022.
key_findings: 732,218 measles cases were reported in China from 2005 to 2022, with a male-to-female ratio of 1.43:1.
The highest incidence was observed in infants under 8 months (75.41 per 100,000), followed by the 0–4 year age group (26.03 per 100,000).
51.18% of all cases occurred in children under 5 years old.
A high-incidence spatiotemporal cluster persisted from 2005 to 2008 (RR=4.69, LLR=140,816, P<0.001), while a low-incidence cluster was detected from 2016 to 2022 (RR=0.08, LLR=113,675, P<0.001).
population: children and general population in China, 2005–2022
limitations: using provincial administrative divisions as spatial units may underestimate clustering and miss localized outbreaks
early reporting system stages may have introduced information biases such as underreporting or misreporting
